subject: Mutual action playbook + decision timeline for Vitalis pilot
messages:
From: rafael.mendes@redwoodai.com
To: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@vitalishealth.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@vitalishealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action playbook + decision timeline for Vitalis pilot

Hi Sofia & Arjun —

Thanks again for a focused conversation earlier. Below is a concise post-call recap and a proposed mutual-action playbook to align milestones, owners, and the approval path. I tried to capture the pain, the success criteria you gave, and the internal stakeholders we discussed. Please correct anything I missed.

Key pain & context
- Current triage and clinical-assist workflows are producing too many false positives, increasing clinician review time (~18% longer per shift).
- On-prem data residency and SOC2 evidence are mandatory for pilot access.
- Your team needs an inference runtime that scales predictably during daily peaks (ED hours).

Stated goals for a successful pilot (30 days)
1) 30% reduction in false positives on triage rules measured on redacted test set
2) <250ms median token latency during simulated peak loads
3) Clear runbook for handoff to Ops with audit logging and retention config

Proposed mutual action playbook (high level)
- Week 1 (Jun 21–27): Pilot onboarding & baseline data ingest — Owners: Vitalis (Sofia, Arjun) + Redwood SRE (Vanessa)
- Week 2 (Jun 28–Jul 4): Model tuning and latency profiling — Owners: Redwood ML (Neha) + Vitalis engineering
- Week 3 (Jul 5–11): Integration tests, security walkthrough, SOC2 artifacts exchange — Owners: Vitalis security + Redwood security (Vanessa)
- Week 4 (Jul 12–18): Acceptance testing and exec review — Owners: Vitalis clinical lead + Redwood AE (Rafael)

Decision path & approvals
- Technical sign-off: Vitalis Engineering (Arjun) with Redwood SRE validation
- Security sign-off: Vitalis Security (Sofia) after SOC2 evidence checklist is confirmed
- Commercial/governance: Procurement issues DOE (estimated by July 20) — we recommend a short statement of work to lock scope (attached draft SOW).

Open asks for you
- Confirm which datasets we should use for the false-positive baseline and who will provide access (S3 or on-prem transfer).
- Confirm SOC2 artifact owner and expected turnaround for evidence (Sofia?).
- Any hard blackout dates in July for clinical staff?

Attachments: Vitalis-SOW-draft-v1.pdf (draft scope & pricing)

Next steps (my suggested cadence)
- I’ll share an updated SOW and a detailed runbook by Thu Jun 17.
- Can we lock a pilot kickoff on Mon Jun 21 at 10:00am PT?

Short summary: Pilot focused on safety-first inference with a clear acceptance metric (false positive reduction) and security gating. We’ll keep latency and cost visible during tuning.

Thanks — looking forward to confirming owners and kickoff.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodai.com
Redwood Inference

---

Adding a few operational clarifications from the Redwood side so procurement has what it needs: 

- Pricing & burst capacity: the attached SOW uses a 30-day reserved pool estimate with a burst allowance; Rafael — if we want to tighten cost estimates I suggest we put a tokenized cap for acceptance tests.
- Data transfer options: we can accept S3 STS role or set up a short-lived VPN tunnel; for SOC2 traceability, S3 with encrypted transfer is preferable.
- Runbook: I’ll draft the initial runbook template (onboarding, keys, KV cache expectations, latency test harness) and push to the shared doc by Thu Jun 17 EOD.

Subject: Finalized mutual action playbook & kickoff (updated timeline)

Sofia / Arjun —

Appreciate the quick turn on the dataset access plan and SOC2 ownership. I’ve updated the playbook with your freeze window and a tightened timeline. High-level changes: 

- Kickoff confirmed: Mon Jun 21, 10:00am PT — calendar invites sent to core team and to procurement placeholder.
- Baseline dataset delivery: Arjun to share S3 access by Wed Jun 16 (we received the initial token this morning).
- SOC2 artifacts: Sofia to share initial package by Jun 25. Vanessa will validate and confirm any missing items by Jun 28.
- Acceptance review target: Jul 15 (exec sync Jul 16) — leaves procurement runway to Jul 20 for sign.

Updated milestones (dates):
- Jun 21: Kickoff + environment provisioning
- Jun 23–27: Baseline ingest & first profiling run
- Jun 28–Jul 4: Latency tuning & model iteration
- Jul 5–11: Integration tests (avoid Jul 7–9 blackout)
- Jul 12–15: Acceptance testing

Attachments included: final SOW draft & completed security questionnaire. Rafael — I’ll create a shared folder for runbook artifacts and put a first-pass test harness there.

If all sounds correct, I’ll: 
1) send a short mutual-action playbook doc with owners and due dates (living doc),
2) ping procurement for a single-line PO placeholder, and
3) schedule weekly check-ins (30 minutes) starting Jun 24.

Confirm and I’ll proceed.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
